chunks: He said: informed me Abu al-Qasim Ja'far son of Muhammad son of Qawlawayh may [Allah] have mercy on Allah he said: narrated to me Muhammad son of 'Abd Allah son of Ja'far al-Himyari he said: narrated to me my father he said: narrated to me Harun son of Muslim he said: narrated to me Mas'adah son of Ziyad he said: I heard Ja'far son of Muhammad upon them both be peace

and indeed he was asked about His saying the Exalted: "So to Allah belongs the argument the decisive" so he said: when it will be the Day of Resurrection will say Allah the Exalted to the servant: Were you a learned person? then if he says: yes, [Allah] will say to him: then why did you not act according to what you knew? and if he says: I was ignorant, [Allah] will say to him: then why did you not learn? thus He will call him to account, and that is the argument the decisive of Allah Mighty and Majestic over His creation.

الْحُجَّةُ الْبَالِغَةُ.context: A Quranic expression (6:149) meaning Allah's irrefutable proof against His creation.

فَيَخْصِمُهُ.context: Allah's irrefutable argument leaves no valid excuse.
فَيَخْصِمُهُ.translation: He will call him to account

يَوْمُ الْقِيَامَةِ.context: The day when all people will be held accountable.

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the decisive argument of Allah (al-hujjah al-balighah) in Quran 6:149 according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) interprets Quran 6:149 ('To Allah belongs the decisive argument') in the context of the Day of Resurrection. Allah will question every person: if they were learned, they will be asked why they did not act on their knowledge; if they were ignorant, they will be asked why they did not seek knowledge. This interpretation was given in the scholarly circles of Kufa during the second Islamic century, where the obligation of seeking religious knowledge was a central ethical teaching. The 'decisive argument' (al-hujjah al-balighah) thus means that no human can excuse themselves before Allah, since both knowledge and the pursuit of knowledge are obligatory.
